body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. You need to onboard a consultant from a partner company who will access a single application in your tenant. The consultant will establish credentials through an emailed link that grants them access to your tenant. You want to use the least privileged access level for the administrator who will perform the onboarding task. Which one?

explanation.correct: The documentation lists the Guest Inviter role as the least-privileged access level for the task of inviting an external guest. This role grants the minimum permissions required to send the invitation link that lets the external person establish their own credentials in the workforce tenant.

perChoice.a: User Administrator is the least-privileged access level for creating a brand new internal account in the tenant, not for sending an invitation link to an external consultant.
perChoice.b: Groups Administrator is the least-privileged access level for creating groups and managing group membership, not for inviting external users.
perChoice.c: Privileged Role Administrator is the least-privileged access level for assigning Microsoft Entra directory permissions to people, not for inviting external guest users.

body.stem:
An administrator needs to create a new Microsoft Entra group that will grant its members access to perform administrative actions in Microsoft Entra ID, rather than assigning such access individually. Your tenant has the appropriate license. Which minimum access level must the administrator hold to enable this capability during group creation?

Planned new group settings:
  Group name: Helpdesk-Admins
  Group type: Security
  Intended use: Grant Microsoft Entra administrative access to its members
  Membership type: Assigned

explanation.correct: The documentation states that enabling the Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group setting (which the planned settings describe) requires at least the Privileged Role Administrator. This setting is only available with P1 or P2 licenses, and turning it on automatically selects Assigned as the Membership type.

perChoice.a: User Administrator grants enough access to create a group, but does not include the ability to enable the Microsoft Entra-assignable setting on the new group.
perChoice.b: Groups Administrator grants enough access to create a group, but cannot enable the Microsoft Entra-assignable setting on the new group.
perChoice.d: Guest Inviter is used to send invitations to external users; it does not provide the access needed to enable Microsoft Entra-assignable on a group during creation.

body.stem:
An administrator created a Microsoft Entra group called Finance-Readers, which has Security as the group type, but the team later realizes they need shared mailboxes, calendar, and SharePoint collaboration features that require the Microsoft 365 group type. You need to convert the group to support these features without losing who currently has access. Which action should you take?

Current group properties:
  Id              : 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-3a2b-1c0d-9e8f7a6b5c4d
  DisplayName     : Finance-Readers
  GroupTypes      : []
  MailEnabled     : False
  SecurityEnabled : True
  MembershipType  : Assigned
  Member count    : 24

options.text: Delete the existing group, then create a new group with Microsoft 365 as the type, and add the original members to the new group
Edit the group's Properties to change the Group type to Microsoft 365
Create a new Microsoft 365 group, then add the existing group as a member of the new group
Enable the Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group setting on the existing group

explanation.correct: The documentation states that the Group type cannot be changed after a group has been created. To switch from Security to Microsoft 365, you must delete the existing group and create a new group with Microsoft 365 as the type, then re-add the people who had access.

perChoice.b: The documentation explicitly states that the Group type cannot be changed after the group is created; editing Properties will not let you switch the group from Security to Microsoft 365.
perChoice.c: Adding the existing Security group as a member of a new Microsoft 365 group does not change the original group's type; the original Security group remains a Security group.
perChoice.d: Enabling the Microsoft Entra-assignable setting on the existing group does not change the group type; it only controls whether Microsoft Entra directory permissions can be assigned to the group.

body.stem: You administer Microsoft Entra ID. You want to set up nested groups, where one existing group becomes a member of another group, so that all of the inner group's people inherit access to any resources granted to the outer group. Review the four groups and their current types shown by the Microsoft Graph command output. Which pair of groups can be nested together as inner member and outer parent?

exhibit.text:
Get-MgGroup -All | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -in 'EngineeringHub','SalesHub','MarketingGroup','CommsChannel' } | Select-Object DisplayName, GroupTypes, MailEnabled | Format-Table -AutoSize

DisplayName        GroupTypes               MailEnabled
------------       -----------               -----------
EngineeringHub     []                        False
SalesHub           []                        False
MarketingGroup     ['Unified']                True
CommsChannel       ['Unified']                True

options.text: EngineeringHub as the inner member and SalesHub as the outer parent
EngineeringHub as the inner member and MarketingGroup as the outer parent
MarketingGroup as the inner member and SalesHub as the outer parent
MarketingGroup as the inner member and CommsChannel as the outer parent

explanation.correct: The documentation states that adding a security group as a member of another security group (nested groups) is supported. EngineeringHub and SalesHub are both Security groups (empty GroupTypes, MailEnabled False), so this pairing is the only supported nested configuration among the four groups in the exhibit.

perChoice.b: The documentation explicitly states that adding security groups to Microsoft 365 groups is not supported.
perChoice.c: The documentation explicitly states that adding Microsoft 365 groups to security groups is not supported.
perChoice.d: The documentation explicitly states that adding Microsoft 365 groups to other Microsoft 365 groups is not supported.

body.stem: You support the help desk of a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. An analyst whose only directory role assignment is User Administrator must remove an account that carries the Global Administrator directory role, but the delete attempt is refused for them. You need to grant the analyst the additional role that lets this removal succeed. Which role should you assign?

rows: Directory role held by the analyst
Result of the analyst's delete attempt

explanation.correct: Only the Privileged Authentication Administrator role can delete any user, including accounts that hold administrative directory roles. A User Administrator is limited to deleting non-admin users, Helpdesk Administrators, and other User Administrators, so the analyst cannot remove the Global Administrator account until this role is added to them.

perChoice.b: Groups Administrator is scoped to managing groups and group membership settings. It carries no permission over deletion of user accounts, so adding it would not unblock the analyst.
perChoice.c: Cloud Application Administrator focuses on application tasks such as managing service principals and enterprise applications; it does not allow user accounts to be deleted from the directory.
perChoice.d: Global Reader grants read-only permissions over directory objects. Read-only roles cannot remove a user, so the delete attempt would still fail.

body.stem: You manage a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. A group is meant to hold the field kiosks of the RetailOps department so that a single assignment of a shared resource can cover all of them. The membership rule you saved for this group is refused at creation time and the group is never populated. You need to revise the rule so the group can be created. Which revision should you make?

exhibit.text:
Group name        : RetailOps-Field-Kiosks
Membership type   : Dynamic membership
Membership rule   : (device.deviceOSType -eq 'Windows10Enterprise') -and (user.department -eq 'RetailOps')
Target objects    : Devices
Validation result : Invalid membership rule, the group was not created

options.text: Remove the user.department condition and keep only the device.deviceOSType condition
Remove the device.deviceOSType condition and keep only the user.department condition
Keep both conditions and add a third condition based on each user's sign-in activity
Keep both conditions but change the RetailOps condition to FieldServices

explanation.correct: A dynamic group is created for either users or devices, never for both, and a rule that targets devices can reference device properties alone; it can't be built on the attributes of the devices' owners. The user.department part of the saved rule inspects a user property, which is why the rule is refused. Dropping that part and building the rule on device.deviceOSType yields a valid device group.

perChoice.b: Removing the device property and leaving the rule built on user.department turns the rule into a user-based rule, so the group would collect people from the RetailOps department instead of the kiosks assigned to them, which isn't what the group is for.
perChoice.c: The rule already fails because it mixes a user property into a device rule; adding another user-related clause keeps that conflict. Sign-in activity is also not a directory attribute that membership rules can evaluate.
perChoice.d: Changing the compared value doesn't change which kind of object the property comes from. The rule still reads a user property inside a device group, so it remains invalid.

body.stem: You onboard new identities into a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. Each task below must be done with the fewest tenant permissions that still allow it. Drag each task to the assignment that meets that requirement.

items.text: Create a new account for a full-time employee in the workforce tenant
Bring in a partner contact from another company so they can work in the tenant
Grant tenant-wide elevated permissions to a new account at the same time it is created

explanation.correct: The least-privileged role differs per onboarding task: the standard account-creation task needs User Administrator, bringing an outside partner into the tenant by email needs Guest Inviter, and handing out tenant-wide elevated permissions as part of onboarding needs Privileged Role Administrator.

perChoice.i1: Creating a new account in a workforce tenant is the basic onboarding task, and the guidance lists User Administrator as the minimum role for it.
perChoice.i2: Bringing in a partner contact from another company is the external B2B invitation task, for which the guidance lists Guest Inviter as the minimum role; User Administrator is not needed for that task.
perChoice.i3: Granting tenant-wide elevated permissions while the account is created means assigning Microsoft Entra roles, and the guidance lists Privileged Role Administrator as the minimum role for that step.

body.stem: You are creating a new account in the Microsoft Entra admin center. On the Properties section of the new user page, you must record the details listed in the table. Drag each detail to the section of that page where it belongs.

rows: Age group of a student in a K-12 district

items.text: Age group of a student in a K-12 district

explanation.correct: The Properties page of the new user flow is split into five categories, and each listed detail falls into exactly one of them: names into Identity, organizational details into Job information, reachability details into Contact information, the school age band into Parental controls, and the worldwide location into Settings.

perChoice.i1: First and last name are entered in the Identity section, which also carries the User type setting.
perChoice.i2: Department and manager are organizational details and are entered in the Job information section, alongside job title.
perChoice.i3: A work phone number is contact information and belongs in the Contact information section.
perChoice.i4: An age band for a pupil in a K-12 district is entered in the Parental controls section, where the age band and any parent consent together drive the legal age group classification.
perChoice.i5: The user's worldwide location is entered in the Settings section of the Properties page.

body.stem: You are provisioning the four accounts described in the table and need to classify each one correctly. The classification decides who manages the credentials and how much access the account gets in your tenant. Drag each account to the user type that matches its facts.

columns: Access the account gets in your tenant
rows: Engineer employed by a sister company
Authenticated by their home tenant through federated sign-in
Signed in with an external method
New hire in your own company

items.text: Engineer employed by a sister company
New hire in your own company

explanation.correct: Classification follows two facts at once: whether the credential lives in your tenant and how much access the account gets. Credentials administered inside your tenant plus full access gives the internal member; credentials in your tenant plus reduced access gives the internal guest; federated sign-in from a home tenant plus full access gives the external member; and an external sign-in method plus reduced access gives the external guest.

perChoice.i1: The account exists in your tenant with tenant-administered credentials but reduced access, which is the internal guest profile: an account in your tenant that carries guest-level privileges.
perChoice.i2: The account is authenticated by its own organization's tenant through federated sign-in and still gets full access in your tenant, which is the external member profile.
perChoice.i3: The account signs in with an external method and receives reduced access, which is the external guest profile: a true guest of the tenant.
perChoice.i4: The account has credentials administered inside your tenant and gets the same access as a full-time employee, which is the internal member profile.

body.stem: You are creating four groups in your tenant and each one has to deliver the access pattern described in the table. Drag each group to the group type that meets its requirements.

rows: Entries added and removed automatically by a rule
Entries added and removed automatically by a rule
People and a service principal that read a shared folder
A manager adds or removes each entry by hand
Shared mailbox, calendar, and SharePoint site
A manager adds or removes each entry by hand

explanation.correct: What the group holds and how it maintains its roster decide the type: a rule-managed roster of field kiosks is a dynamic membership group for devices, a rule-managed roster of employees matched on department is a dynamic membership group for users, hand-managed access to a shared folder for people plus a service principal is a security group, and a shared mailbox and calendar for non-employee volunteers is a Microsoft 365 group.

perChoice.i1: Field kiosks managed by a rule call for the device-based dynamic group: it adds and removes hardware as device attributes change, and a dynamic group can only target devices or users, never both.
perChoice.i2: Employees matched on a user attribute such as department call for the user-based dynamic group, which adds or removes them automatically as their attributes change.
perChoice.i3: Granting access to a shared folder to people plus a service principal, with membership handled by hand, fits the security group used to manage access to shared resources; only security groups can hold service principals as members.
perChoice.i4: A shared mailbox, calendar, and SharePoint site for volunteers from outside the organization is the collaboration scenario the Microsoft 365 group is built for; a group email address is also only offered for this type.

body.stem: Four resources in your tenant receive access in four different ways. You need to name the mechanism the resource owner used in each case. Drag each scenario to the access pattern it represents.

items.text: You add one person straight to the resource's own permission list yourself
You assign a group to the resource, so every current and future member of it receives the access
You build a group from attributes on people's records, and the resource owner decides which attribute values qualify
You assign a group to the resource, but the roster of that group is maintained by a system outside Microsoft Entra, such as an on-premises directory or a SaaS app

explanation.correct: Access can reach a resource in four distinct ways. Putting a single person on the resource yourself is direct assignment; assigning a group so all of its current and future members receive the access is group assignment; building a group from attributes on people's records so the owner decides which values qualify is rule-based assignment; and assigning a group whose roster is maintained by an outside system is external authority assignment.

perChoice.i1: The resource owner places the person on the resource themself, with no group involved, which is the pattern where the owner assigns the user to the resource.
perChoice.i2: The resource owner assigns a group to the resource and every member of that group gets the access, which is the pattern where the resource owner assigns a group instead of listing people.
perChoice.i3: The resource owner builds a group driven by attributes on individual user records and maintains the conditions that decide who qualifies, which is the rule-driven pattern.
perChoice.i4: A group is still assigned to the resource, but the roster comes from an outside source such as an on-premises directory or a SaaS app rather than from Microsoft Entra ID, which is the external-source pattern.

body.stem: You administer a Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. An employee has left the company, so you removed the person's account and it no longer appears on the All users page. HR tells you the person might be rehired in a few weeks, and finance wants to know what happens to the licenses the account was holding. Which retention period applies?

rows: Microsoft 365 E3; Microsoft Entra ID P1

body.statement: The removed account can still be restored from the Deleted users page for {{retention}} days, and the licenses it was consuming are released so that other users can take them.

explanation.correct: Once an account is deleted it stops showing on the All users page, but it remains available on the Deleted users page for 30 days and can be restored during that window. Deleting the account also frees up the licenses it was using so they can be assigned to other users.

perChoice.retention:a: Seven days is far shorter than the supported window; a rehired employee returning after a week or two would find the record already purged.
perChoice.retention:b: Fourteen days also falls short of the supported window and would leave no recovery path for anyone returning later in the month.
perChoice.retention:d: Ninety days overstates the window; once the supported period ends the deleted record is purged and can no longer be restored.

body.stem: A group in your tenant is populated automatically from your on-premises identity store through Microsoft Entra Connect. An administrator edited that group's members in the Microsoft Entra admin center, and the edit was undone at the next synchronization cycle. You now need to change the membership so the change sticks. Which system of record should you make the change in?
body.statement: Membership for the synchronized group must be changed in {{system}}.

explanation.correct: Field-Kiosks takes its membership from your on-premises identity store, and groups synchronized from on-premises Active Directory can only be managed there. Membership edits made in the cloud are overwritten on the next synchronization cycle, so the change must be made in Windows Server Active Directory and then synchronized in.

perChoice.system:b: This is where the lost edit was already made. Because the group is synchronized, changes entered here are not authoritative and are reverted when synchronization runs again.
perChoice.system:c: The Exchange admin center is where distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups such as All-Hands are managed, not a group whose members come from the on-premises system.
perChoice.system:d: This is the other supported place for mail-enabled groups; it still cannot hold the membership changes for a group that is synchronized from on-premises.

body.stem: A group in your tenant hands its members a directory-wide administrative permission, and today people are added to it one at a time by hand. The team now wants that membership maintained automatically by a rule. You open the group's Properties page, switch the membership setting to the rule-based option, and the change does not stick. Which setting on this group is causing that?

rows: Items editable on the Properties page
Group name; Group description; Group type; Membership type; Object ID

body.statement: The change is blocked because this group was created with {{setting}}.

options.text: Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group
Self-service group creation can be enabled for the group
A group expiration policy can be applied to the group
A group naming policy can be applied to the group

explanation.correct: Enabling the Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group option during creation forces the membership type to Assigned, and a group in that state can no longer have its membership type edited. That is why switching to the rule-based option on the Properties page has no effect.

perChoice.setting:b: Self-service group creation governs who may create new groups in the tenant; it does not lock the membership type of an existing group.
perChoice.setting:c: A group expiration policy controls automatic deletion of a group that has gone unused for a set period; it has no effect on which membership options can be selected.
perChoice.setting:d: A group naming policy blocks restricted words and enforces naming consistency for group names; it does not prevent the membership type from being changed.

body.stem: You are creating a new account in the Microsoft Entra admin center and are on the Assignments tab of the New user page, where a colleague has listed the group memberships, the directory role grants, and the administrative unit placement requested for this person. You would like to finish everything in this single pass rather than come back afterwards. Which statement describes what this page supports?
body.statement: On this page you can select no more than {{maxItems}} groups or roles for the new account, and the account can be placed in only {{auItems}} administrative unit.

explanation.correct: The Assignments tab lets you pick up to 20 groups or roles while the account is being created, but a user can only be placed in a single administrative unit at that point. The 13 group and role items in the request fit under the ceiling, while the second administrative unit has to be added after the account exists.

perChoice.maxItems:a: A ceiling of five would block legitimate requests such as the nine groups listed here, so it is too restrictive.
perChoice.maxItems:b: Ten is also lower than the supported maximum and would stop a request of the size shown from being completed in one pass.
perChoice.maxItems:d: There is a documented maximum; the selection from this page is capped rather than unlimited.
perChoice.auItems:b: Two administrative units cannot be selected while the account is created; only one may be chosen, so the second placement is a follow-up task.
perChoice.auItems:c: Three administrative units is well beyond what the creation page allows; it accepts a single placement only.
perChoice.auItems:d: Four administrative units likewise exceeds the single placement permitted during account creation.

body.stem: You are creating one group in your Microsoft Entra workforce tenant. It has to carry the same badge-reader access policy for three different kinds of directory objects at once, so that assigning the policy once to the group covers all of them. Which group type should you create?

columns: Directory object that must be covered by the policy
rows: Badge readers BR-114, BR-115 and BR-116

body.statement: You should create a {{groupType}} so that a single assignment of the policy reaches all three kinds of objects.

explanation.correct: Of the group types available in Microsoft Entra ID, only a security group can hold all three of the listed object kinds: members of a security group can include users, devices and service principals. Assigning the badge-reader policy once to that group therefore covers the readers, the two staff accounts and the app registration together.

perChoice.groupType:a: Members of a Microsoft 365 group can only be users, so the badge readers and the BadgeSync app registration could not be placed in this group and would never receive the policy.
perChoice.groupType:b: A dynamic membership group for devices adds and removes devices automatically from device attributes, and its rules can only reference device attributes. It cannot hold the two user accounts or the app registration.
perChoice.groupType:c: A dynamic membership group for users adds and removes users automatically from user attributes. Devices and service principals never become members, so the badge readers and the app registration would be left without the policy.

body.stem: You invited a partner specialist into your Microsoft Entra workforce tenant two days ago. The account now exists in your directory, but the person has not signed in and you want to send them another message so they can finish setting up their access. Which action should you take?

rows: Days since the message was sent

options.text: Select Resend invitation from the B2B collaboration tile on the user's details page
Select Reset password from the user's details page
Delete the account and send a new invitation from the New user page
Set Account enabled to No and then back to Yes on the user's details page

explanation.correct: An external guest creates their own credentials from the message they receive, so until they accept, the account sits at PendingAcceptance. In the Microsoft Entra admin center you open the invited guest user, go to the B2B collaboration tile on their details, and use Resend invitation to send the message again. That is the documented way to reissue the message while the state is PendingAcceptance.

perChoice.b: Resetting a password does nothing for this situation: an external guest chooses their own password from the message they received, and resetting a password is not the recovery step for an invitation that has not been accepted.
perChoice.c: Deleting the account throws away the existing invitation and forces a new invitation from scratch, which is unnecessary when the guest has simply not accepted yet; the supported action is to send the message again from the user's details.
perChoice.d: Toggling Account enabled only controls whether the account can sign in. It sends nothing to the person and does not change the state of the invitation, so the guest would still never receive a message.

body.stem: You are creating one group in your tenant for the marketing department. It must carry its own address so members can send mail to it, and it will be used as the team's collaboration space for shared documents. On the New group page, which Group type should you select?

columns: Field on the New group page

explanation.correct: Choosing the Microsoft 365 Group type is what turns on the Group email address field, so the address marketing@contoso.com can be typed during creation, and Microsoft 365 groups are the ones that provide collaboration opportunities. The planned values on the page can then be entered as listed.

perChoice.b: A security group is used to manage access to shared resources. The Group email address option is only available for Microsoft 365 group types, so that field won't be offered for this selection.
perChoice.c: Distribution lists are managed in the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft 365 admin center rather than through the group creation options here, and they don't provide the Group email address field on the New group page.
perChoice.d: A mail-enabled security group remains a security group used for access to shared resources; like any security group type, it isn't offered the Group email address option, which is limited to Microsoft 365 group types.

body.stem: Your team is creating a new Microsoft Entra group in the Microsoft Entra admin center and wants to capture only the fields the page actually requires. Each field on the New group page plays a different role: some must be filled in, some can be left blank, and one only shows up under a certain Group type. Drag each field to the role it plays.

slots.label: Must be filled in or the group cannot be saved
Must be chosen and also controls which other fields are visible
Can be left blank and the group is still saved without it
Only visible when a specific Group type is chosen

explanation.correct: On the New group page you must choose a Group type and supply a Group name before the group can be saved. The Group type choice also gates which other fields are visible because choosing Microsoft 365 enables the Group email address option, while that option is not shown for Security groups. The Group description is documented as optional, so leaving it blank does not prevent the group from being created.

perChoice.name: Goes in 'Must be filled in or the group cannot be saved' because the New group page requires a unique Group name and rejects names that start with a space.
perChoice.grouptype: Goes in 'Must be chosen and also controls which other fields are visible' because Group type is a required choice, and selecting Microsoft 365 turns on the Group email address option.
perChoice.description: Goes in 'Can be left blank and the group is still saved without it' because the New group page lists Group description as an optional field.
perChoice.email: Goes in 'Only visible when a specific Group type is chosen' because the Group email address option appears only after Microsoft 365 is selected as the Group type.

body.stem: You help run a customer tenant through cross-tenant delegated administration. Every time you use New group there, the request is refused and no group ends up in the directory. Which option should you take?

rows: Create a new group in the customer tenant
Group naming policy in the customer tenant
Prefix: [department of group creator]- , Suffix: none

body.statement: To get the group created in the customer tenant, you should {{action}}.

options.text: Create the group from an administrator account in the target tenant
Create the group from an administrator account in the calling tenant
Rename the group from an administrator account in the target tenant
Assign the group from an administrator account in the target tenant

explanation.correct: The group guidance notes that group creation by GDAP administrators isn't supported when the target tenant uses a group naming policy prefix or suffix that references attributes of the calling user, such as department or company name, and it directs you to use an administrator account in the target tenant to create the group. The exhibit shows exactly that combination: delegated administration plus a prefix built from the caller's department, so the documented path is to run the creation from an administrator account that lives in the target tenant.

perChoice.action:b: The calling tenant is your own home directory, not the customer directory that needs the group. A group created there lives in the wrong directory, and it leaves the attribute-based prefix in the customer tenant untouched, so the delegated create attempt there would still be refused.
perChoice.action:c: Nothing was created, so there is no group to rename. The request is refused at the moment of creation, before a group object with any name exists.
perChoice.action:d: There is no group yet to assign to anything, and assignment isn't the goal here. The refusal happens when the group is created, so an assignment step can never run for it.
